title.zh: 胸廓：一只会呼吸的笼子
title.en: The Ribcage: A Cage That Breathes

text.zh: 胸口这一圈骨头有个难题：既要硬到能挡住撞击，又要软到每分钟能张开十几次。
text.en: The ring of bone around your chest faces a contradiction: hard enough to take a blow, yet supple enough to open a dozen times a minute.

text.zh: 12 对肋骨从脊柱向前包过来，一根根斜着向下。吸气时它们被提起，整圈就往外扩了一圈。
text.en: Twelve pairs of ribs sweep forward from the spine, each slanting downward. Lift them as you breathe in, and the whole ring widens.

text.zh: 正前方是胸骨，一块扁平的长骨。心肺复苏按压的位置，就在它下半段。
text.en: Straight in front lies the sternum, a flat blade of bone. The spot pressed during CPR is on its lower half.

text.zh: 肋骨并没有直接长到胸骨上，中间隔着一段肋软骨。这段软的，正是胸廓能张开的原因。
text.en: The ribs never reach the sternum directly; a length of costal cartilage bridges the gap. That soft segment is exactly why the cage can open at all.

text.zh: 后方每一根肋骨都挂在一块胸椎上。12 对肋骨、12 块胸椎，一一对应，一个不多一个不少。
text.en: At the back, every rib hangs from a thoracic vertebra. Twelve pairs of ribs, twelve vertebrae — matched one to one, with none left over.

text.zh: 肋骨之间填着肋间肌，它们才是拉动这只笼子的绳索。骨头负责形状，肌肉负责动。
text.en: Between the ribs sit the intercostal muscles, the ropes that actually work this cage. Bone supplies the shape; muscle supplies the movement.

text.zh: 笼子里装的是心脏。它偏在正中略左的位置，前面正好有胸骨和肋软骨挡着。
text.en: Inside the cage sits the heart, set just left of centre, with the sternum and costal cartilages standing guard directly in front of it.

text.zh: 左肺只有两叶，就是为了给心脏让位。同一个空间里，两个器官各自迁就了对方的形状。
text.en: The left lung has only two lobes, precisely to make room for the heart. Sharing one space, each organ has given way to the other's shape.

text.zh: 所以胸廓不是一副静止的盔甲，而是一只每天开合两万次、还要顺便护着心肺的笼子。
text.en: So the ribcage is no static suit of armour, but a cage that opens and closes twenty thousand times a day while guarding the heart and lungs besides.
